messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: sev2 - routing anomalies detected between hosted and dedicated pools for tenant namespace 'acme-io'. Error rate spike (5xx) across region-us-west-2 and automated fallback loops observed. Paging oncall/sophia.

sophia: seeing it, joining. quick summary?

dan: customers reporting increased latency and occasional 503s. traffic from hosted is spilling into dedicated pools but some requests are routing back to hosted, creating back-and-forth. looks like policy shim introduced yesterday may be misclassifying namespace labels.

priya: confirm: the routing policy change from yesterday was the new "namespace-shim" that maps tenant namespaces to capacity-tiers via a regex label. I pushed it at 03:14 UTC.

mike: logs showing model variant mismatch errors during cross-pool handoff: `VariantNotCompatible: model-v2a != model-v1q` and eviction storms. snippet: ```ERROR 2026-03-15T03:47:12Z routing_engine: route failed: VariantNotCompatible tenant=acme-io src=hosted pool=d0 -> dst=dedicated-pool-7```

kevin: also seeing region fallback loop entries: requests pin to us-west-2, then fallback to us-east-1 because capacity-check returned false, then some heuristic sends back to us-west-2. repeated for same request id.

infra-bot: automitrigger: set routing-policy to read-only rollback if available. Current policy commit: 4f8b9c (namespace-shim).

priya: rolling policy back now to previous commit (4f7a3d). executing `deployctl rollback routing-policy 4f7a3d`

lex: oncall, should we isolate acme-io to prevent more cross-bind? we can add a temporary tenant-isolation rule to keep hosted -> hosted only till stable.

sophia: yes. prioritize customer impact mitigation over keeping routing behavior. lex do the isolation; dan and mike prepare rebalancing.

lex: applying emergency ACL: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/override -d '{"tenant":"acme-io","mode":"isolate","from":"hosted","to":"hosted"}'` -> response 200.

mike: isolation applied. starting pool drain for any in-flight to dedicated. running: `scripts/drain_pool.sh dedicated-pool-7 --tenant acme-io`

dan: started drain. also increasing eviction thresholds on dedicated-pool-7 to avoid TTL-based churn: `cfg set dedicated-pool-7.eviction.threshold 0.12` 

priya: rollback in progress, control plane reports policy rollback completed at commit 4f7a3d. verifying routes...

mike: still seeing a small subset of sessions stuck in loop due to cached template in routing-proxy. need to restart proxy on edge hosts in us-west-2 for tenant acme-io.

kevin: /roll restart routing-proxy --selector region=us-west-2 --filter tenant=acme-io  (careful: do canary 3 hosts first)

lex: canary restart on 3 hosts succeeded. no increased errors observed. proceeding with rolling restarts.

oncall: handed off to ops (sophia) for mitigation window. 

incident-bot: Severity update: impact reduced to degraded (latency, intermittent 5xx for small percentage) after isolation + rollback. Notifying CS to contact affected customers.

priya: root cause (preliminary): namespace-shim regex was too permissive and matched a broader set of tenant labels that share the 'acme' prefix; combined with variant compatibility check missing in shim caused wrong pool mapping. fix: tighten regex and add variant compatibility check in routing decision.

sophia: action items: 1) permanent policy fix (priya) 2) add unit/integration tests for variant check (dan) 3) add a preflight dry-run stage for policy updates (kevin) 4) postmortem (lex). assigning and ETA in-thread.

priya: filing PR now: `PR #4823` with stricter regex and variant check. linking tests and rollout plan.

dan: adding regression test: `tests/test_routing_variant_compat.py` with simulated hosted->dedicated flows. will land by EOD.

kevin: I'll add preflight gating to the policy deploy pipeline; will mock check against current model catalog and tenant map. target next sprint.

mike: dedicated-pool-7 drained and rebalanced. returning capacity to normal in us-west-2. no further spillbacks for last 6 minutes.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations in place. plan: keep isolation rule for 1 hour, then gradually un-isolate after deploying PR and tests. Postmortem requested.

lex: I'll start the postmortem doc and invite CS to include customer timeline.

sophia: thanks team. continuing monitoring for 30 mins then hand back to oncall regular cadence. :thumbsup:
